version.changelog:
talkies 1.3.5

- Updated documentation in SKILL.md: clarified security and file staging notes, improved explanations of shared file handling and authentication defaults.
- Removed skill-card.md file.

llm.summary: The skill is clearly documented for a self-hosted speech service, but its shared file-staging API can expose and irreversibly delete other callers' staged media if the server is not tightly controlled.

dimensions.detail: Auth is optional and disabled when TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN is unset, private-network URL download blocking is disabled by default, and staged uploads or cached URL downloads persist indefinitely on the server.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses Docker images, a persistent data bind mount, and optional CUDA support. The setup examples are straightforward, but the server binds broadly unless the operator restricts Docker port mapping.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill warns agents to only read or delete files staged in the current user-approved workflow, but the documented API itself has a shared namespace where any caller with API access can list, read, and delete staged files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Staged files and downloaded URL cache entries persist until explicit deletion, DELETE /v1/files/{path} is irreversible, and administrative unload endpoints can disrupt other users' model state on shared deployments.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ASR/TTS purpose is coherent and the shell, network, Docker, ffmpeg, and curl usage fits setup and transcription workflows. The skill also exposes server-side file staging, URL caching, model unload endpoints, and voice cloning, all disclosed as sensitive capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only against a Talkies server you operate or explicitly trust. Set TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN, restrict network exposure, avoid staging sensitive media on shared instances, do not use GET /v1/files for browsing, and delete only files created for the current task. Treat URL downloads, debug logging, voice cloning, and model unload commands as admin-level or consent-sensitive actions.
llm.findings: [TM1] unexpected: The finding is supported in context: /v1/files is documented as a shared, unisolated staging bucket with list/read/delete access for any API caller, no per-caller ownership, optional auth, and no automatic expiration. The skill does disclose guardrails, so this is a Review concern rather than evidence of malicious intent.
